persistence_invariants.brief: Additive migration on the pre-existing stock_records table: it adds nullable batch_number + serial_number. A single-step downgrade drops ONLY those two columns while every pre-existing row persists, and a re-upgrade re-adds them (additive round-trip with row preservation, since the table pre-exists from F1). ISOLATION REQUIREMENT: this round-trip verification MUTATES the schema (alembic downgrade -1, then re-upgrade) and MUST be exercised on its OWN isolated ephemeral migration branch (a schema-mutating / @pytest.mark.migration test), NOT against the shared post-migration verify database. A downgrade run on the shared branch would drop batch_number/serial_number and corrupt the post-migration schema that every other F6 test (AC1 backfill, AC2 NULL-survival, AC3 probe, AC4 location) depends on — those would then fail with 'column batch_number does not exist' on an otherwise-correct migration.

The expand migration adds the two columns and backfills them from inventory_code within one transaction: either every pre-existing row is present with columns added and conforming rows backfilled, or the migration does not commit — no torn/partial state and no dropped row (realizes R1 at the migration boundary).

S2 contract migration on the pre-existing stock_records table: the up migration DROPs inventory_code (batch_number + serial_number remain). It is reversible as a round-trip — a single-step downgrade RECONSTRUCTS inventory_code and repopulates it by recomposing location-batch-serial joined with the delimiter (the mirror of S1's decomposition, per OD1), leaving location canonical/unchanged; a re-upgrade re-drops inventory_code returning to the dropped end state (AC1, AC3, AC4). Since the table pre-exists and the drop removes only a column, every pre-existing row PERSISTS across the round-trip with location/batch/serial unchanged (data-preservation is legitimate here — this is a column drop on a pre-existing table, not an initial create_table). ISOLATION REQUIREMENT: this verification MUTATES the schema (drop, then downgrade/re-upgrade) and MUST be exercised on its OWN isolated ephemeral migration branch (@pytest.mark.migration), NOT against the shared post-migration verify DB — the shared branch has inventory_code already dropped, and downgrading it there would corrupt the schema every other test depends on.

The S2 contract migration drops inventory_code atomically: either the column is fully removed with all pre-existing rows present and their location/batch_number/serial_number unchanged, or the migration does not commit — no torn state, no dropped or corrupted row (AC2, realizes R1 at the contract boundary). Verified by seeding rows then applying the drop on an isolated ephemeral migration branch (schema-mutating).

open_decisions.question: What composes the combined inventory_code, and is its leading segment authoritative for location? (F1 deferred this as OD2-inventory-code-composition.)
open_decisions.resolution: inventory_code is a hyphen-delimited location-batch-serial string of VARIABLE width (split on '-': segment 2 = batch_number, segment 3 = serial_number; codes like 'X-1' or a bare 'c' have no batch/serial segment). The leading segment is NOT authoritative for location — the canonical location column (part of UNIQUE(sku,location) from F1) stays unchanged (AC4). Consistent with F1, which already stores location as its own column; no contradiction with any gated F1 AC.

open_decisions.question: Rows whose inventory_code does not parse are left with NULL batch_number/serial_number (AC2). Do these rows require a remediation/backfill-correction path BEFORE the S2 contract story drops inventory_code (which permanently discards the original code, the only source of the unparsed batch/serial), or is a NULL-forever state acceptable? The integrity-probe count (AC3) exists precisely to gate that decision.
open_decisions.resolution: NULL-forever is accepted: S2 proceeds with the drop of inventory_code WITHOUT a remediation/backfill-correction path — none of S2's ACs (AC1-AC4) gate the drop on the integrity-probe being zero or introduce a correction step, so a non-conforming row keeps its NULL batch_number/serial_number and simply survives the drop unchanged (AC2). Consistent with S1, which deliberately stored NULL for non-parsing rows and supplied the integrity-probe count as visibility, not as a hard gate; no gated S1 AC required remediation before contract. Documented lossiness of the reverse path: for a NULL-batch/serial row the down migration (AC3) can only recompose from the canonical columns it has, so such a row round-trips to a location-only inventory_code rather than its original combined string — acceptable because inventory_code is not part of the accepted end state (AC4) and the original code is intentionally discarded by the contract step.

nfrs.fitness_function: the F6 expand migration preserves every pre-existing stock_records row (no loss/corruption) and is reversible as a round-trip; verified against the paired Lakebase branch.
fitness_functions: the F6 expand migration (adding batch_number + serial_number and backfilling from inventory_code) preserves every pre-existing stock_records row: post-migration the row count is unchanged and no row is dropped or corrupted (R1, AC2).

the expand migration is reversible as a round-trip: a single-step downgrade drops only the two added columns while every pre-existing row persists, and a re-upgrade re-adds them (PI1). This clause MUTATES schema and MUST be verified on its own isolated ephemeral migration branch (schema-mutating / @pytest.mark.migration), never against the shared post-migration verify DB that the other F6 tests depend on.

S2-contract-migration: the contract migration that DROPS inventory_code preserves every pre-existing stock_records row (row count unchanged, no row dropped or corrupted, per-row location/batch_number/serial_number unchanged) — realizing R1 (no silent data loss) at the CONTRACT boundary (PI4, AC2). Distinct from the expand clauses above (which cover the S1 add/backfill side): this covers the S2 drop side. Verified by seeding rows then applying the drop on an isolated ephemeral migration branch (schema-mutating / @pytest.mark.migration); the covering S2 test (T17/PI4 or T18/PI3) MUST carry nfr_id NFR-R1-migration-data-survival.

nfrs.fitness_function: the F6 expand migration weakens no existing write-time guarantee: after migrating, the CHECK(quantity >= 0) on stock_records still rejects a negative quantity and the no-overcommit rule is untouched (F6 adds no write/pick path; it must only preserve R2, not re-implement it).

the F6 migration preserves UNIQUE(sku, location): after adding batch_number/serial_number and backfilling, no two rows share (sku, location) and a duplicate write is still rejected. Batch and serial become separately addressable WITHOUT altering the canonical (sku, location) identity (AC4).

the F6 migration + integrity-probe suite runs against the paired Lakebase branch via DATABASE_URL (Alembic applied to the branch first), not a mock or in-memory substitute; CI refuses to merge a PR whose integration tests do not run against a real branch.

the split batch_number and serial_number are exposed as distinct JSON fields by the boundary (not server-rendered HTML) and rendered as separately addressable fields in the single-page React + TypeScript client wherever the combined code was shown before.

the migration and probe read the DB connection from DATABASE_URL in the environment (no hard-coded connection string; the substrate-provisioned databricks_postgres name is left untouched); enforced by the config-in-env gate.
